video.title: Chris Makes BA's Best Lasagna | From the Test Kitchen | Bon Appétit
video.description:
Join Chris Morocco in the Bon Appétit Test Kitchen as he makes BA's best lasagna. Why in the world would we tell you to make meatballs, brown them, and then break them into pieces—for a ragù? Sounds crazy, but it’s the best way we found to sear a big batch of meat without overcooking it. This MeatballMethod™ yields deep color (a.k.a. flavor) along with tender meat. If you want to use fresh pasta, go for it, you overachiever you. We also tested the recipe with no-boil noodles, but found they soak up a lot more sauce and the lasagna loses its wonderful ooziness; instead, we recommend the regular dried stuff.heck out the recipe here: https://www.bonappetit.com/recipe/ba-best-lasagna

Want Bon Appétit shirts, hats and more? https://shop.bonappetit.com/?utm_source=youtube&utm_brand=ba&utm_campaign=aud-dev&utm_medium=video&utm_content=merch-shop-promo

Still haven’t subscribed to Bon Appétit on YouTube? ►► http://bit.ly/1TLeyPn

Want more Bon Appétit in your life? Subscribe to the magazi

### **Tab 3: 🔥 Chris's Pro Tips** (Info Grid)

**The MeatballMethod™**
🔥 Form meat into meatballs and sear in two batches. This creates massive color on all sides without overcrowding. Steam escapes through gaps. Superior browning + tender meat (it finishes braising, not searing).

**Tomato Paste Alchemy**
🔥 Toast the paste in oil BEFORE adding liquid. The oil's high temperature cooks out the raw edge and concentrates flavor. Add it directly on aromatics, let it fry for ~2 minutes — this is non-negotiable.

**Flour Roux Magic**
🔥 Toast the flour in butter for ~2 minutes. There's incredible flavor development. Then whisk milk in vigorously and crank heat to boil — starch must boil to fully thicken.

**Béchamel's Secret**
🔥 There's an alchemy to pasta cooked with béchamel that cheese alone can't replicate. Béchamel creates creaminess and allows pasta to buckle up and get crispy like a cracker — that's the magic of traditional lasagna.

**Layer Thin, Not Thick**
🔥 Five thin layers of everything beat three massive layers. Vary pasta direction with each layer so sheets interlock and overlap. Better texture, better integration.

**Fresh Pasta, Not No-Boil**
🔥 Use fresh egg pasta lasagna sheets (like d'Zcecho), NOT no-boil. Fresh pasta absorbs flavor and creates superior texture. No-boil is a trap.

**Pasta Water Discipline**
🔥 Add sheets one-by-one and stir constantly — they really, really stick. Don't keep them in water longer than necessary or they'll absorb too much and become mushy. Lay on parchment immediately.

**Ragù Timing**
🔥 Low and slow at 225°F for 2.5–3 hours. Lazy simmer, not aggressive boil. After ~2 hours, break up meatballs with a potato masher. The sauce reduces and concentrates; flavors meld.

**Fond Is Flavor**
🔥 When searing meatballs, don't scorch the fond (brown bits) on the bottom — that's where the flavor lives. Let them sit and develop color; don't force browning.

**The Rest Is Essential**
🔥 Resist the urge to serve ripping hot. Let the lasagna rest 10 minutes so all liquid and elements rebalance. You'll get a clean, held-together slice and won't burn your mouth.

## **Verdict & Summary**

**⭐ Rating: 5/5**
Chris's BA Best Lasagna is **the definitive traditional Italian-style lasagna** — deep flavor from the meatball-seared ragù bolognese, silky béchamel, and perfectly layered fresh pasta. The MeatballMethod™ solves browning efficiency. The 2.5–3 hour low braise creates a sauce so rich and concentrated it tastes like it took all day. The béchamel creates a creaminess no amount of cheese can replicate.

**Why This Works:**
- ✅ **The MeatballMethod™** — sear, break, braise. Superior color + tender meat + efficient browning.
- ✅ **Tomato paste alchemy** — toasted in oil before liquid, concentrating flavor.
- ✅ **Proper béchamel** — flour toasted, milk boiled to thicken, nutmeg and cayenne traditional.
- ✅ **Fresh egg pasta** — absorbs sauce, creates superior texture. No-boil is a trap.
- ✅ **Five thin layers** — better texture and integration than three thick layers.
- ✅ **Low braise** — 225°F for 2.5–3 hours. Lazy simmer allows flavors to meld.

**Best For:** Home cooks wanting to master traditional lasagna bolognese. Weekend project with big payoff. Freezes beautifully once made.

**Time Investment:** ~45 min active prep, 3.5 hours hands-off braising, 1 hour assembly and baking = ~5 hours total, but mostly oven time.

**Difficulty:** Medium — no advanced techniques, just patience and precision.
